# NTAP (NetApp, Inc.) — Technical Analysis Report
**Analysis date: 2026-10-07 | Verified close: 235.24 (open 231.48, high 237.54, low 230.31, volume 3.00M)**

## Executive Summary

NTAP is in a powerful, accelerating uptrend. The stock has rallied from ~180 at the start of September to 235.24 on 2026-10-07 — roughly +30% in five weeks — with the last four sessions alone adding ~10% (209.61 → 225.76 → 223.27 → 227.94 → 235.24). Every indicator is confirming bullish structure, but momentum and volatility gauges now flash elevated overbought/extension warnings. This is a trend-strength environment, not a mean-reversion entry.

## Trend Structure

- **Full bullish alignment.** Price (235.24) > 10 EMA (217.46) > 50 SMA (195.41) > 200 SMA (139.76). The distance to the 200 SMA (~68% above) confirms a mature, well-established long-term uptrend; the steep gap to the 50 SMA (~20% above) shows the rally has recently accelerated beyond even medium-term trend.
- **10 EMA slope is vertical.** The 10 EMA rose from ~186.5 on 09-04 to 217.46 on 10-07 — the fastest-moving average is doing the work of carrying the breakout. As long as closes hold above ~217, the short-term momentum regime is intact.
- **Recovery from the September shakeout.** The data shows a choppy two-week consolidation (09-01 to 09-10, closes 180–188) including a violent 09-03 session (open 161.59, close 184.96, volume 6.23M — the period's highest). Price then broke out on 09-11 (198.83 close) and has not looked back. That low-volume pullback resolved upward, which is textbook continuation behavior.

## Momentum

- **MACD is strongly positive and expanding.** MACD line = 10.32, signal ≈ 6.89, histogram = +3.43 — the histogram has risen every session since 09-22 and is at its widest reading in the window. No bearish divergence: MACD just made a new high alongside price, matching the August peak (~11.0 on 08-17) on a much higher price level.
- **RSI = 77.88 — overbought.** RSI has been above 70 for three of the last four sessions (70.13, 75.93, 74.81, 77.88). In a strong trend RSI can stay pinned high, so this is a caution flag rather than a sell signal — but it does mean fresh longs are buying into statistically stretched conditions. Notably, the August RSI peak (~76.7) preceded the late-August pullback from ~207 to ~180.

## Volatility & Bands

- **Price is above the Bollinger upper band.** Close 235.24 vs. upper band 233.07 — the second consecutive session of closes near/above the band (227.94 vs. 227.75 on 10-06). Band-riding is characteristic of strong trends, but combined with RSI >77 it signals short-term exhaustion risk is elevated.
- **ATR = 8.56, rising.** Daily volatility is elevated and ticking up (7.73 on 10-01 → 8.56 on 10-07). For risk management: a 2× ATR stop from the close sits near 218 — almost exactly the 10 EMA. That is the logical invalidation level for momentum longs.
- **Volume confirms.** Breakout sessions on 10-02 (5.06M) and the up-days since carried above-average volume (~3.0M vs. a ~2.2M typical day), supporting the move rather than suggesting a low-participation drift.

## Key Levels (verified data)

- **Support:** 233 (upper band, now potential pivot), ~225.8 (10-02 breakout close), ~217.5 (10 EMA / 2×ATR stop zone), ~203.8 (Bollinger mid / 20 SMA).
- **Resistance:** none overhead — price is at all-period highs for this window; 237.54 (10-07 intraday high) is the immediate level.
- **Invalidation:** a close back below ~217 (10 EMA) would break the steep momentum regime; below 203.8 (Bollinger mid) the breakout thesis fails.

## Actionable Takeaways

- **Trend-following:** The trend is unambiguously up with expanding MACD and volume confirmation — momentum longs remain valid while price holds the 10 EMA (~217).
- **Entry discipline:** RSI ~78 and a close above the upper band argue against chasing at 235+. Better risk/reward entries are pullbacks toward 225–218.
- **Risk:** Elevated ATR (8.56) means wide stops and smaller position sizes are appropriate. A volatility-driven retracement of 5–8% toward the 20 SMA (~204) would be normal even within a continuing uptrend.
- **Watch for:** MACD histogram contraction, RSI bearish divergence on the next price high, or a high-volume reversal day — the August pattern (RSI ~76 → ~13% pullback) is the relevant precedent.

## Summary Table

| Category | Indicator | Latest (verified) | Signal |
|---|---|---:|---|
| Price | Close 2026-10-07 | 235.24 | All-period high, extended |
| Trend | 10 EMA | 217.46 | Price above — steep short-term uptrend |
| Trend | 50 SMA | 195.41 | Price ~20% above — strong medium-term trend |
| Trend | 200 SMA | 139.76 | Price ~68% above — mature long-term uptrend |
| Momentum | MACD / Signal / Hist | 10.32 / 6.89 / +3.43 | Bullish, expanding, no divergence |
| Momentum | RSI | 77.88 | Overbought — caution on new entries |
| Volatility | Bollinger Upper | 233.07 | Close above band — extension, band-riding |
| Volatility | Bollinger Mid / Lower | 203.84 / 174.61 | Mid = key pullback support |
| Volatility | ATR | 8.56 | Elevated/rising — size positions accordingly |
| Levels | Support | 233 / 225.8 / 217.5 / 203.8 | Pivot, breakout, 10 EMA, 20 SMA |
| Levels | Resistance | 237.54 (intraday high) | No overhead structure — price discovery |

**Bottom line:** Strongly bullish trend with verified momentum confirmation, but short-term overbought (RSI ~78, above upper band). Favor buying pullbacks to 217–225 over chasing; invalidation on a close below ~217.

# NTAP (NetApp, Inc.) — Fundamental Research Report
**As-of date: 2026-10-07** · All figures USD millions unless noted · Source: SEC EDGAR filings available on or before 2026-10-07

## 1. Data availability caveat

The fundamentals vendor withheld profile-level data (market cap, valuation multiples, 52-week range, sector) for this date to avoid look-ahead bias, and insider transactions were withheld because the vendor cannot establish which trades were public as of 2026-10-07. This report therefore rests on as-filed SEC financial statements — the quarterly income statement, balance sheet, and cash flow statement — through the quarter ended **2026-07-31** (NetApp's fiscal Q1 FY2027, fiscal year ends late April).

## 2. Company profile

NetApp, Inc. is an enterprise data infrastructure company — hybrid-cloud storage arrays, all-flash systems, and cloud data services. Revenue is a mix of product (hardware/storage systems) and recurring software/services. Its economics are characterized by structurally high gross margins (~70%) and heavy, consistent capital return via buybacks and dividends.

## 3. Recent-quarter earnings (income statement)

| Quarter ended | Revenue | Gross profit | Op. income | Net income | Diluted EPS |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2025-07-25 | 1,559 | 1,098 | 309 | 305 | 1.15 |
| 2025-10-24 | 1,705 | 1,227 | 399 | 334 | 1.51 |
| 2026-01-23 | 1,713 | 1,209 | 434 | 375 | 1.67 |
| 2026-04-24* | ~1,700s est. | — | — | — | — |
| 2026-07-31 | **2,025** | **1,419** | **484** | ~375+ | **1.88** |

*The 2026-04-24 column is absent from the served income statement (filing-gap artifact), but balance sheet and 9-month cash flow rows confirm it was reported.

Key observations:

- **Record revenue.** Q1 FY2027 revenue of $2,025M is the highest quarterly print in the entire 17-year series — prior peak was $1,713M (Jan 2026). Sequential growth of ~18% QoQ and ~30% YoY vs. the year-ago July quarter ($1,559M) is a dramatic acceleration vs. the flat ~$1.5–1.7B range of the prior four years. This magnitude of step-up is consistent with AI-related storage demand and/or a major product-cycle win.
- **Margins holding.** Gross margin ~70% (1,419/2,025) — in line with the ~68–70% structural norm. Operating margin expanded to ~24% (484/2,025), best in the series alongside the Jan-2026 quarter.
- **EPS trajectory strong.** Diluted EPS of $1.88 vs. $1.15 a year ago (+63% YoY). Trailing four reported quarters (Oct-25, Jan-26, Apr-26 est., Jul-26) imply annualized EPS well above $6, a record run-rate.
- Note: Q3 FY2018 shows a one-time −$479M net income / −$1.79 EPS (tax-reform-related charge) — historical, not relevant to current operations.

## 4. Balance sheet

| Item | 2025-07-25 | 2025-10-24 | 2026-01-23 | 2026-04-24 | 2026-07-31 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Total assets | 8,989 | 10,823 | 9,679 | 9,630 | 9,971 |
| Cash & equivalents | 1,511 | 2,742 | 2,085 | 2,072 | 1,629 |
| Total liabilities | 7,994 | 9,783 | 8,704 | 8,644 | 8,813 |
| Stockholders' equity | 995 | 1,040 | 975 | 986 | 1,158 |

- **Thin equity base by design.** Equity of ~$1.0–1.2B against ~$10B of assets reflects decades of buybacks exceeding retained earnings. Debt-to-equity is meaningless here; the balance sheet is leverage-tolerant only because cash generation is extremely reliable.
- **Cash position $1.63B** — adequate liquidity; the drawdown from $2.7B (Oct-25) partly reflects a heavy buyback quarter (see below) and seasonal working capital.
- Current ratio is comfortable: current assets $5,672M vs. current liabilities $4,568M at 2026-07-31.
- The Oct-2025 balance sheet spike ($10.8B assets, $9.8B liabilities) appears to be a transient working-capital/financing item that normalized by Jan-2026.

## 5. Cash flow & capital return

- **Operating cash flow remains powerful**: $503M in Q1 FY2027 alone; FY2026 OCF ≈ $1,117M (9M through Jan-26: $800M + Q4). FY totals have run $800M–$1.2B for years — a dependable ~$1B annual OCF machine.
- **Capex is trivial** ($102M in Q1 FY27; ~$150–200M/yr) — asset-light model, so nearly all OCF is free cash flow.
- **Financing outflows dominate**: −$319M in Q1 FY27, and FY totals of −$1.2B to −$1.8B in recent years — the surplus is returned via buybacks and dividends rather than hoarded. Q4 FY2026 financing was notably large (−$1,157M in the Apr-2026 quarter implied), explaining the cash drawdown.
- Investing flows are mostly investment-portfolio shifts (purchases/maturities), not M&A of note in the recent window.

## 6. Insider transactions

Withheld by the vendor for this as-of date — no insider signal can be reported without look-ahead risk.

## 7. Trader takeaways

- **Bullish fundamental momentum**: the Jul-2026 quarter is a clear inflection — record revenue, record EPS, stable ~70% gross margins, expanding operating leverage. If the AI-storage demand thesis holds, estimate revisions likely moved up through this print.
- **Cash engine intact**: ~$1B+/yr OCF, minimal capex, aggressive buybacks shrinking the share count and compounding EPS growth.
- **Watch items**: (a) whether the $2B+ revenue quarter is repeatable or a pull-forward spike — check guidance language in the Aug-2026 earnings; (b) low absolute cash ($1.6B) against high current liabilities — fine while OCF holds, fragile if a downturn hits; (c) thin equity means buyback pace, not leverage capacity, is the constraint on capital return.
- **Valuation unknowable from this data** — multiples were withheld; another agent with price data must weigh whether the re-acceleration is already priced.

| Cash flow | OCF $503M in quarter; ~$1B+/yr run rate | Positive |
| Capital return | Financing outflows −$1.2 to −$1.8B/yr (buybacks + dividends) | Positive for EPS, limits cushion |

Bull Analyst: # Bull Case: NTAP (NetApp, Inc.) — Opening Argument

Let me make this simple: NTAP just printed the best quarter in its 17-year filing history, broke out to record highs on an institutional upgrade, and is riding the single biggest spending wave in enterprise tech — AI data infrastructure. The bear hasn't spoken yet, so let me lay out the case and then pre-empt the obvious objections.

## The Fundamental Inflection Is Real

This isn't a momentum story pasted onto a flat business. Look at what actually happened in the July 2026 quarter (FQ1 FY27):

- **Revenue $2,025M** — a series record, up ~30% YoY vs. $1,559M a year ago and ~18% sequentially. For context, NTAP revenue had been stuck in a $1.5–1.7B band for four straight years. A $300M+ step-change in one quarter is not noise — it's a demand inflection.
- **EPS $1.88, up 63% YoY.** Operating margin hit ~24%, the best in the series alongside January. This is operating leverage, not just top-line stuffing.
- **Gross margin held ~70%** through the acceleration — the growth isn't coming at the cost of pricing power.
- **FY27 guidance of $7.975–8.225B revenue / $9.73–10.03 EPS** (per the Aug 27 8-K) confirms management sees this as durable, not a one-quarter pull-forward.

And this is an asset-light cash machine underneath it all: ~$1B+/year operating cash flow, capex of only ~$100–200M, and financing outflows of $1.2–1.8B/yr going straight back to shareholders via buybacks and dividends. Buybacks on a shrinking share count compound that EPS trajectory mechanically.

## The Narrative and the Tape Agree

The Evercore ISI upgrade to Outperform didn't create the rally — it validated it. Price action confirms: +30% in five weeks, breakout above the prior $232 high on above-average volume (~3.0M vs ~2.2M typical), MACD expanding with no bearish divergence, and every moving average in bullish alignment. Retail flow on StockTwits is 3-0 bullish with zero bearish voices, and the "Intelligent Data Infrastructure for the AI era" framing from Insights 2026 gives the move a fundamental story, not just a chart.

Storage is a picks-and-shovels AI trade. Every hyperscaler capex dollar and every enterprise AI deployment needs somewhere to put the data. NTAP re-rating from "legacy storage vendor" to "AI data infrastructure platform" is exactly the kind of multiple expansion story that runs for quarters, not days.

## Pre-empting the Bear

I can hear the objections coming, so let me deal with them:

**"RSI is 78, it's overbought, it's above the Bollinger band."** True — and irrelevant to the thesis. Overbought is a timing flag, not a valuation argument. In strong trends RSI stays pinned; the August precedent (RSI ~77 → ~13% pullback) is exactly why I'd say *buy the dip, don't short the rip*. Pullbacks to the 217–225 zone are entries. A stock that never pulls back is the one you regret not owning.

**"The revenue spike might be a pull-forward."** Possible, but the burden of proof is on that claim. Guidance was raised, margins held, and the sequential pattern (1,559 → 1,705 → 1,713 → ~1,700s → 2,025) shows acceleration, not a spike-and-fade. Plus the AI storage demand curve is early — peers like PSTG are telling the same story.

**"Sentiment is thin — one source, 16 messages."** Fair, but sentiment being thin doesn't make it wrong; the labeled flow that exists is unanimously bullish and the institutional catalyst (Evercore) is verifiable. I'd rather have a real upgrade and a record high than a fat Reddit thread.

**"Thin equity, low cash."** That's decades of deliberate buyback policy, not distress. $1.6B cash, current assets $5.7B vs current liabilities $4.6B, and $503M of OCF in a single quarter. This balance sheet is fragile only if OCF collapses — and OCF just set records.

## Bottom Line

NTAP has the rare trifecta: a genuine fundamental inflection (record revenue/EPS, raised guidance), a structural tailwind (AI data infrastructure), and technical confirmation (breakout to highs on volume with institutional sponsorship). The bear will talk about overbought charts and data gaps — I'll talk about a company that just grew revenue 30% and EPS 63% while returning billions to shareholders. Momentum plus fundamentals beats momentum alone. The trend is your friend until the close below ~217 says otherwise — and nothing in the fundamentals suggests that's coming.

Your move, Bear.

Bear Analyst: # Bear Case: NTAP (NetApp, Inc.) — Rebuttal

Nice speech, Bull. You gave us a victory lap dressed up as an investment thesis. Let me be the one in the room who reads the fine print: you're buying a stock +30% in five weeks, ~68% above its 200-day average, at RSI ~78, on the back of one quarter that even the fundamentals desk flagged as possibly a pull-forward — and you're calling that a "trifecta." I call it peak euphoria pricing a fragile story as fact.

## The "Record Quarter" Is One Data Point, Not a Trend

Let's look at your crown jewel: $2,025M revenue in FQ1 FY27. You're right that it's a record — and that's precisely the problem. NetApp spent four years bouncing in a $1.5–1.7B band, then printed a number ~18% above the prior quarter and ~30% above the year-ago period in a single step. In enterprise hardware, jumps of that magnitude have two classic explanations:

1. **Pull-forward demand** — large AI-related orders landing in one quarter, draining the next two. The fundamentals report itself flags exactly this: "whether the $2B+ revenue quarter is repeatable or a pull-forward spike" is listed as a watch item, not a settled fact.
2. **Sector beta, not idiosyncratic strength** — and here's a receipt you skipped: on 2026-10-05, during a storage-sector rotation day, NTAP fell -2.7% while WDC rallied +6.3% and STX +4.9%. If NetApp were truly the AI-storage winner being re-rated, it would lead the sector on rotation days, not lag it by nine percentage points. Part of this move is the tide, not the boat.

You said "the burden of proof is on the pull-forward claim." No — the burden of proof is on whoever pays $235 for a business that was a $1.6B/quarter company twelve weeks ago. The buyer of the anomaly bears the burden. And note: the very next print (late November, FQ2) is the event that resolves this. You're buying weeks before the single most binary data point in the thesis, with zero margin of safety in the price.

## The Guidance Trap — Including Misquoted Guidance

You cite FY27 guidance of $7.975–8.225B / $9.73–10.03 EPS as confirmation of durability. Two problems:

- **The market is already trading as if the high end is a lock.** Implied full-year revenue at the midpoint (~$8.1B) requires the $2B+ run-rate to hold every quarter. Guidance ranges get set conservatively; the stock price doesn't. If FQ2 prints ~$1.9B — still healthy, still up YoY — the stock gets de-rated anyway because the bar is now "repeat the anomaly."
- **The sentiment report documents active misinformation**: AI-generated summaries are circulating wrong FY27 guidance numbers, and a StockTwits poster had to correct the record against the actual 8-K. Your retail "conviction" is partly built on fabricated numbers. That's not a bull point.

## Valuation Is a Black Box — and That's a Bear Point

Here's what your argument carefully avoided: **no valuation multiples exist in this dataset.** The fundamentals vendor withheld market cap, P/E, EV/EBITDA — everything. So your "re-rating story that runs for quarters" is a claim about multiple expansion with no knowledge of the current multiple. NTAP has historically traded as a value-ish storage name at low-teens earnings multiples. If it's now trading at 25x+ on peak earnings, you're not buying a re-rating — you're buying the completed re-rating at its most extended technical moment in the window. Arguing "the multiple will expand" while the stock is 68% above its 200 SMA is arguing to buy what's already been bought.

## The Technical Picture You Dismissed Is the Risk
